justification: Standard: two real behaviour changes to a live, deployed API endpoint's DB-write and connection lifecycle. Not Critical because the blast radius is narrow (no frontend caller for this endpoint was found anywhere in this repo, so today's real-world traffic is unproven) and both changes are contained to the same three DB-helper functions, verified twice over -- once as fast mocked unit tests (default pytest run) and once as opt-in real-database integration tests that actually connect to production Supabase (PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 -m database).

pre_impl.existing_data: drawdown_verify_audits table -- confirmed live 2026-09-04 to NOT exist in production (DQ-91), re-confirmed again by tests/test_drawdown_verify_real_db.py's own real-DB assertion. This PR does not create it (a production DDL write was blocked by the session's own auto-mode classifier and needs explicit user approval) -- it stops the API from lying about the outcome, and stops leaking a connection per call, while the table is still missing.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: None new for the fail-closed fix (the pre-existing code already assumed _insert_audit could fail). The connection-leak fix corrects an assumption that was simply wrong: `with _db_conn() as conn:` was assumed to close the connection on exit: psycopg2 connections only COMMIT/ROLLBACK in __exit__, never close -- confirmed against the real driver, not just documentation, by test_drawdown_verify_real_db.py.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to every new request from merge onward. No historical rows are affected -- there is nothing to backfill, since the table has never held any rows.
pre_impl.external_source_error: N/A -- no new external source call added. Note: _submit_hyp3_job (the real HyP3/ASF Earthdata call) is deliberately NOT exercised by any test in this PR, mocked or real -- it is a paid third-party job submission with 1-2 hour turnaround, not something that belongs in an automated suite. That remains genuinely untested end-to-end; flagged rather than silently absent.
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A -- no frontend caller found for this endpoint in this repo.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Audit-write silent lie (before this PR): caller receives 200 'submitted' with a non-functional fallback ID while the audit record silently does not exist. Connection leak (also pre-existing, found by the pre-push adversarial scanner while this PR already had the file open): every call to _insert_audit/_update_audit/_get_audit opened a psycopg2 connection against the pooler and never closed it -- including the polling endpoint, which can be hit repeatedly over a 1-2 hour job. After this PR: audit-write failure returns 500 with an explicit message and the hyp3_job_name for reconciliation; every DB helper closes its connection on every exit path, proven against a real connection, not just a mock's approximation of one.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_drawdown_verify_audit_failclosed.py -v (mocked, runs in default CI) AND PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 python -m pytest -m database tests/test_drawdown_verify_real_db.py -v -o addopts= (opt-in, actually connects to production Supabase)
falsifiable_check.fails_when: Both suites were run against the fix REVERTED (git stash push -- services/drawdown_verify.py, keeping the tests, then git stash pop to restore) -- proven twice, once mocked and once against the real driver and real production data, not assumed either time.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: MOCKED (first attempt): 2 of 4 fail-closed tests went RED with 'DID NOT RAISE HTTPException'. MOCKED leak tests (first attempt): 3 of 4 failed for the WRONG reason ('DID NOT RAISE') because the default MagicMock.__enter__ returns a different object than the mock itself, unlike real psycopg2 -- caught mid-session, fixed by pinning mock_conn.__enter__.return_value = mock_conn, re-run: all 4 then failed cleanly with 'AssertionError: Expected close to have been called once. Called 0 times.' REAL-DB (against actual production, actual Supabase pooler): test_get_audit_closes_the_real_connection_even_though_the_table_is_missing failed with 'AssertionError: finally: conn.close() did not fire on the real connection when the real query genuinely failed' -- this is a genuine UndefinedTable error from the real missing drawdown_verify_audits table, and a genuine unclosed psycopg2.extensions.connection object, not a simulation of either. After git stash pop restoring the fix: all 8 mocked tests and all 3 real-DB tests pass; the real connection's .closed attribute reads nonzero and reusing it raises a genuine psycopg2.InterfaceError.

After: caller gets a 500 naming the failure and the hyp3_job_name for manual reconciliation; the HyP3 job itself is NOT cancelled (documented in the new code comment) so it is not silently wasted, just not auto-tracked.

The polling endpoint (GET .../drawdown-verify/{job_id}) can be hit repeatedly over a 1-2 hour job, so this compounds per job.
break_it.what_happens: Before: pool exhaustion risk under any real traffic. After: every helper closes its connection via try/finally on every exit path, proven against a REAL psycopg2 connection to production (not a mock) via tests/test_drawdown_verify_real_db.py, which uses the actual missing-table error as its real failure trigger.

break_it.scenario: Sol cross-review (round 2, on push): the 500 error message asserted 'This request has NOT been recorded', a certainty the exception cannot actually give -- PostgreSQL could commit the row and the connection could still drop before the acknowledgement reaches this code, in which case the row exists despite the exception.
break_it.what_happens: A caller (or a human doing manual reconciliation from the error text) could wrongly conclude a row that actually exists does not, and skip checking for it.
break_it.how: services/drawdown_verify.py -- reworded to 'could not be confirmed' / 'UNCONFIRMED', explicitly stating the ambiguity rather than asserting an absence. Tests updated to match (test_audit_insert_failure_raises_500_not_a_fake_success).

break_it.what_happens: Duplicate paid third-party job submissions on retry, with no way to detect or reconcile them from this table alone.
